# technitium_record_txt (Resource)

Manages a single `TXT` record in an authoritative zone.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The record's domain name, for example `www.example.com`. Use the zone name for a record at the zone apex.
- `zone` (String) The authoritative zone that holds the record.

### Optional

- `character_strings_base64` (List of String) The text as base64 encoded character strings, instead of `text`.
- `comments` (String) Comments stored with the record.
- `disable` (Boolean) Disable the record without deleting it. Defaults to `false`.
- `expiry_ttl` (Number) Deletes the record automatically this many seconds after it was last modified. Terraform then creates it again on the next apply.
- `split_text` (Boolean) Split `text` into separate character strings at each new line.
- `text` (String) The record text. Set either this or `character_strings_base64`.
- `ttl` (Number) The record TTL in seconds. Defaults to the default record TTL in the server settings.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# zone/domain/character_strings_base64/text/split_text, empty values left unset
terraform import technitium_record_txt.hello home.example.com/hello.home.example.com//hello/

# or a JSON object of identity attributes, for values containing "/"
terraform import technitium_record_txt.spf '{"zone":"home.example.com","domain":"home.example.com","text":"v=spf1 ip4:192.168.178.0/24 -all"}'
```
